skills.Set up my collection: Find approved sources, setup progress, actor and next link.
skills.Check my catalog: Read roster and groups, verify eligible inventory and specific stay quotes.
skills.Find demand opportunities: Diagnose sellable capacity, pace and demand; recommend one intervention.
skills.Understand guest conversion: Interpret funnel stages and use scoped analytics to investigate.
skills.Email past guests: Select a consented audience, prepare a draft and approve dispatch.
skills.Manage paid ads: Read ads, prepare a paused Google campaign and control spend.
skills.Review campaign results: Compare email and ad results; preserve windows, channel, visits and attribution bases.

create_email_draft.description: Preview or save a draft for an explicit audience, subject and body. Draft only. Draft preflight also returns sender readiness.

create_paused_google_campaign.description: Preview or confirm creation of a paused Google campaign.

enable_google_campaign.description: Preview or confirm enabling spend for an existing Google campaign, within the current budget.

get_ads.description: Read an ads report for one collection. Choose report sections. Google supports all sections. Meta supports account health and provider-reported attribution in this fixture. Use include_archived for archived campaigns or refresh_health for a current Google health check. For grouped, sorted, or campaign-filtered terms, use get_ads_search_terms.

get_ads_demand_window.description: Read seasonal advertising demand by window.

collection_slug.description: A collection you have access to.

channel.description: Ad channel. 'google' (default) or 'openai' (ChatGPT Ads). The demand read is the same; the click-month return exists for Google only.

days.description: How far back to read landings and price checks (default 90). Bookings from those sessions count whenever they land.

months.description: How many click months to report the return for (default 3).

include_receipts.description: Include every booking behind the cohort table (default false; the table alone is usually enough).

get_ads_search_terms.description: Read paginated Google paid search terms with campaign, grouping and sorting filters.

collection_slug.description: A collection you have access to.

campaign_id.description: Optional Google campaign id (the numeric id from the campaign resource name) to restrict to one campaign.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous page (nextCursor).

group_by.description: Row granularity. 'term_campaign' (default): one row per query per campaign. 'term': one row per query across campaigns. 'ad_group': Google's raw rows.

collection_slug.description: A collection you have access to.

days.description: The window in days ending today: 7, 30 (default, the page default) or 90. The delta compares against the window of the same length before it.

get_campaign_stats.description: Read email campaign delivery, clicks and clicked-to-session results.

get_catalog_groups.description: List collection groups or inspect one group.

get_catalog_properties.description: Read the catalog roster, optionally filtered by property ID, slug or published status. Request detail fields for one property.

get_collection_status.description: Read one authorized collection status section. booking_readiness returns imported, quotable and bookable counts and blockers. email_sender returns sender verification, time checked and next step for a collection-owned domain; email module and ADMIN required. Read only.

get_data_dictionary.description: Discover available scoped analytics views and columns.

get_open_capacity.description: Read sellable capacity over stay dates.

collection_slug.description: A collection you have access to.

group_slug.description: Optional group (VRGroup) slug — restricts to its member homes.

dow.description: Night filter: weekend = Friday + Saturday nights. Default all.

slice_by.description: Aggregation grain. Default total. home: one slice per home (key = home id, home = {id, name, slug}), ordered by open nights, most open first.

get_setup.description: Read outstanding Setup steps and next-action links.

get_stay_quote.description: Price one dated stay and report completeness.

collection_slug.description: Slug (or id) of a collection you can access.

property_slug.description: Slug of the property within that collection (from search_properties).

pets.description: Pets on the stay. Default 0, which prices no pet fee and says so; pass the real count for a pet-friendly home.

list_my_collections.description: List accessible collections, roles and module activation.

pause_google_campaign.description: Preview or confirm pausing an existing Google campaign.

preview_audience.description: Preview eligible audience size, without saving or sending.

run_readonly_sql.description: Read-only analytics against permitted manager views; excludes unauthorized collections and gated data.

query.description: A single read-only SELECT or WITH query over the mgr_insight_v_* views.

params.description: Positional parameters for $1, $2, … in the query (use these for values).

limit.description: Row cap (default 1000, max 10000). Auto-applied if the query has no LIMIT.

dry_run.description: If true, validate the query (EXPLAIN) without executing it.

include_staging.description: Default false. The content-events view returns production traffic only; rows from staging, development, preview and local hosts are excluded so they never inflate guest counts. Set true ONLY to verify a smoke, then filter on the environment column yourself.

save_audience.description: Preview then confirm persistence of a guest audience.

confirm.description: Must be true to write. Omit for a dry-run preview.

schedule_email_campaign.description: Preview or confirm sending an existing draft now or later, excluding guests without marketing consent.

search_properties.description: Search bookable inventory with dated criteria.

collection_slug.description: Slug (or id) of a collection you can access to search within.

dateWindows.description: Up to 5 date windows to check availability and pricing across. Each window returns per-property availability. Omit for browse mode — browse results carry the nightly anchor "from" price only, never a dated total.

budgetMaxPerNight.description: Max nightly budget in major currency units

propertyTypes.description: Property type(s). The coarse family (house vs apartment) is the only hard filter; a specific subtype (e.g. "cabin", "a-frame") returns its whole family with that subtype boosted — cross-manager interleaving may still rank other family members above it; never zero results.

locality.description: Filter by city/town name (e.g., ["Stowe"], ["Seaside", "Cannon Beach"]). Case-insensitive.

country.description: Filter by ISO alpha-2 country code (e.g., "US")

nearLat.description: POINT MODE: Latitude to search near

persona.description: Soft ranking signal — boost properties popular with a guest persona (e.g., "hiking", "romantic", "young_family", "pet_owners", "fishing", "luxury"). Does NOT hard-filter.

feature.description: Soft ranking signal — boost properties with a guest-confirmed feature (e.g., "mountain_views", "spotless_clean", "hot_tub", "cozy", "beachfront"). Does NOT hard-filter.

semanticFilters.description: Reserved optional evidence-backed semantic criteria that complement the explicit location, date, capacity, pet, property-type, and budget filters. Put true must-haves in `required`; put preferences that should improve ranking without excluding otherwise valid stays in `requested`. Until server instructions announce that semantic matching is enabled, omit this field.

required.description: Natural-language must-haves. Every returned property must have listing, policy, amenity, or review evidence for each criterion; never infer a match from missing data.

requested.description: Natural-language preferences used as soft ranking signals. A property may still be returned when one or more requested preferences are not evidenced.

filters.description: The audience rule. All fields optional and combinable (AND). Rolling fields re-resolve at every evaluation, so a saved rule stays evergreen.

vrSlugs.description: Comma-separated property slugs — qualifying stay at ANY of them.

channel.description: Comma list of booking channels the qualifying stay used: DIRECT, AIRBNB, VRBO, BOOKING_COM, EXPEDIA, KISMET, OTHER.

minBedrooms.description: Qualifying stay at a home with >= N bedrooms.

minParty.description: Party size on the qualifying stay (set min=max for exact).

windowAnchor.description: What the stayedFrom/To (or rolling) window keys on: 'stay' = check-in date (travel season), 'booked' = booking date (purchase cadence — e.g. booked ~1 year ago).

stayedDaysAheadFrom.description: Rolling window start = today + N days (negative = past).

stayedDaysAheadTo.description: Rolling window end = today + N days.

stayedYearsBack.description: Shift the rolling window back N years.

minSpendCents.description: Lifetime spend >= N cents (or per-stay with spendBasis).

lastStayBefore.description: Last stay strictly before YYYY-MM-DD (lapsed guests).

notBookedSince.description: Rolling "not rebooked": last stay before today — excludes anyone with an upcoming reservation.

crossBrand.description: Only cross-brand guests (stays span 2+ family collections, or the same profile appears in a sibling collection).

clvBand.description: Return-likelihood band (CLV v0), AFTER the recency modifier: likely = ≥35% of guests like this one book again within a year · possible = 15–35% · low = <15%. Scored per row by the same scorer as the guestbook chip and get_guest.stats.clv (never a second model). Rows the model cannot score (no paying stay / too little history) match no band. Combine with minSpendCents for "who is worth winning back".

clvModifier.description: The FACT that overrides the band: lapsing = last stay >14 months ago and nothing booked (the win-back signal) · returning_booked = a future stay is on file (they ARE returning — usually exclude from win-back sends) · none = neither. Rolling by construction — nothing to drift.

party.description: Count a stay for the whole travel party, not only the booker: true matches anyone recorded on the reservation (booker, companions, primary guest). Applies to stay clauses (windows[] with event 'stay', and stayedFrom/To); booking-date clauses stay the booker's. Set it on the rule-level filters and every part inherits it. A has-clause matches anyone who was on a matching stay; a none-clause excludes anyone who was. Use it for past-guest sends ("everyone who stayed last winter"). Default off.

windows.description: Composable has/none clauses — the power grammar. Example rewarming pair: [{"kind":"has","event":"booked","window":{"fromDays":-364,"toDays":-343}},{"kind":"none","event":"booked","window":{"fromDays":-343,"toDays":0}}].

window.description: A time window: absolute (from/to dates) OR rolling (fromDays/toDays offsets resolved against today at every evaluation; NEGATIVE = the past; yearsBack shifts whole years). Either end may be open.

fromDays.description: Rolling start = today + N days (negative = past).

yearsBack.description: Shift a rolling window back N whole years ("this window, last year").

booked.description: Second window on the SAME reservation's BOOKING date (stay clauses only) — the personal booking-anniversary coupling. Example: {"kind":"has","event":"stay","window":{"from":"2025-12-26","to":"2026-01-04"},"booked":{"fromDays":-371,"toDays":-364}} = "their New Year's stay was booked this week last year" — each week a fresh cohort rolls in, so an always-on send lands in each guest's own booking week. Shift the offsets back to fire early.

fromDays.description: Rolling start = today + N days (negative = past).

yearsBack.description: Shift a rolling window back N whole years ("this window, last year").

minLeadDays.description: Booking lead-time habit: a qualifying stay was BOOKED at least N days before its own check-in (vendor booking time). minLeadDays: 180 = long-lead planners — reach them around their booking anniversary, months before the season. Rolling by construction.

maxLeadDays.description: Upper lead bound: maxLeadDays: 30 = spontaneous bookers — the audience for gap-fill flash offers. Combine with minLeadDays for a band.

shopperDays.description: Live demand: an active journey at this collection within the last N days — the search_guests-composable form of list_shoppers. "Repeat guests shopping RIGHT NOW" = minStays: 2 + shopperDays: 7, the highest-value moment the CDP can name.

emailEngagedDays.description: Campaign-email engagement: opened or clicked a campaign email in the last N days (the SendGrid webhook + open-pixel stamps). "Warm but not booked" = emailEngagedDays: 14 + notBookedSince: true.

customFilterIds.description: Named SQL-backed rules (create_custom_filter) referenced by id. Each one INTERSECTS with the rest of the rule (narrow-only). Prefer the grammar fields; reach for a custom filter only when the grammar cannot say the slice.

parts.description: Named, described, individually toggleable slices of the rule (AND by intersection). PREFER 2-4 small parts over one flat filter bag: every part renders as a chip with its description as the hover card, and the operator toggles each independently. Each part needs name (≤80 chars), description (1-3 sentences a MARKETER understands — what it matches and why it is here; no counts, they go stale), and filters with at least one predicate. Note: parts intersect as separate evaluations, so two parts may be satisfied by different reservations — use ONE part (or a windows clause with match) when criteria must hold on the SAME stay.

description.description: The part explained to a marketer in clear language — the hover-card copy.
